questions.q: Why would a plain SUM(fct_subscriptions[amount_usd]) with no filters produce a wrong MRR number?
options: It would produce exactly the correct number -- there's no real problem with a plain SUM here
fct_subscriptions does not contain an amount_usd column
SUM() cannot be used on a currency column in DAX
It would include cancellation events and revenue from already-cancelled subscribers, both inflating the total incorrectly
questions.explain: Without filtering to revenue-generating event types and currently-active subscribers, a plain SUM adds up every event ever recorded, badly overcounting.

questions.q: What two conditions does the MRR measure's CALCULATE filter on?
options: Only event_type, with no subscriber status filter
event_type IN {"signup", "upgrade"} and dim_subscribers[cancelled_at] = BLANK()
Only subscriber status, with no event type filter
event_timestamp falling within the current calendar year
questions.explain: Both filters are necessary -- excluding cancel-type events and restricting to currently-active subscribers (cancelled_at is blank).

questions.q: Why does the Churn Rate measure use DIVIDE() instead of a plain / operator?
options: DIVIDE() returns BLANK() instead of an error when the denominator is zero, which matters when there's no historical baseline yet
Plain division is not supported in DAX at all
DIVIDE() automatically rounds the result to two decimal places
DIVIDE() is faster to compute than a plain division operator
questions.explain: A plain / would error on a zero denominator (e.g., the dashboard's first month with no prior baseline); DIVIDE() handles that gracefully.

questions.q: What would forgetting the OR condition in Active Subscribers Start of Month's filter cause?
options: It would cause a DAX syntax error
It would overcount active subscribers and understate churn
It would have no effect on the result at all
It would undercount the denominator and overstate the churn rate
questions.explain: Without the OR (catching both never-cancelled and cancelled-after-month-start subscribers), the denominator would be too small, making churn rate look artificially high.

questions.q: Why is fct_subscriptions described as event-grained rather than subscriber-grained?
options: It has one row per signup, upgrade, or cancel event -- not one row per subscriber per month
Grain doesn't apply to fact tables, only dimension tables
It has one row per calendar day regardless of subscriber activity
It has exactly one row per subscriber, identical to dim_subscribers
questions.explain: Understanding fct_subscriptions' actual grain (one row per event) is exactly what makes the CALCULATE filters in the MRR measure necessary -- mixing up grain is a classic source of silently wrong DAX measures.
